title: Pre-derived adjunction from essentially constant derived systems
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with derived categories $D(\mathcal A)$ and $D(\mathcal B)$ and localization functors $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$, $Q':K(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be additive functors with $G$ left adjoint to $F$; additivity is automatic for adjoints between abelian categories. Write $F_h,G_h$ for their componentwise induced functors on homotopy categories and $a_h:G_h\dashv F_h$ for the induced adjunction. Let $K\in K(\mathcal A)$ and $M\in K(\mathcal B)$. The category of quasi-isomorphisms $s:K\to I$ with commuting triangles is filtered, and the category of quasi-isomorphisms $t:P\to M$ is cofiltered. Suppose the diagram $s\mapsto Q'F_h(I)$ is essentially constant as an ind-object with value $RF(K)$ [def-pc-essentially-constant-ind-diagram], and $t\mapsto QG_h(P)$ is essentially constant as a pro-object with value $LG(M)$ [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram]. For any chosen representing cocone $p_s:Q'F_h(I)\to RF(K)$ and cone $u_t:LG(M)\to QG_h(P)$ satisfying those essential-constancy conditions, there is a unique canonical bijection $e:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(Q'M,RF(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(LG(M),QK)$ characterized, for every $s,t$ and $f:P\to F_h(I)$, by $e(p_s\circ Q'(f)\circ Q'(t)^{-1})=Q(s)^{-1}\circ Q(a_h(f))\circ u_t$. This bijection is functorial in both localized variables on the subcategories where the partial derived functors are defined: for morphisms $k:QK\to QK'$ and $m:Q'M'\to Q'M$, and their induced maps $r:RF(K)\to RF(K')$, $l:LG(M')\to LG(M)$, one has $e'(r\circ h\circ m)=k\circ e(h)\circ l$. The induced maps are characterized by compatibility with all fraction representatives: whenever $Q(s)$ followed by the left fraction $(a,s')$ represents $k$, $p_s$ followed by $r$ equals $Q'F_h(a)$ followed by $p_{s'}$; dually, whenever the right fraction $(t',a)$ followed by $Q'(t)$ represents $m$, $l$ followed by $u_t$ equals $u_{t'}$ followed by $QG_h(a)$.

proof.text: Since $RF$ is defined at $K$, the ind-system $I\mapsto F(I)$ indexed by arrows $s:K\to I$ is essentially constant with value $RF(K)$. Applying the essential-constant ind Hom-colimit formula gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(M,RF(K))\cong\varinjlim_{s:K\to I}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(M,F(I))$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 0FND proof (line 9515), first equality

proof.text: For each $I$, morphisms in the right localization are computed, since the quasi-isomorphisms of the homotopy category form a multiplicative system, by the colimit over arrows $t:P\to M$: $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(M,F(I))\cong\varinjlim_{t:P\to M}\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal B)}(P,F(I))$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 0FND proof (line 9515), second equality

proof.text: The two indexing categories are independent, so the iterated colimits can be interchanged canonically, yielding $\varinjlim_s\varinjlim_t\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal B)}(P,F(I))\cong\varinjlim_t\varinjlim_s\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal B)}(P,F(I))$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 0FND proof (line 9515), third equality

proof.text: The underived adjunction $G\dashv F$ gives a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal B)}(P,F(I))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(G(P),I)$ for every $P$ and $I$; applying it inside both colimits gives the corresponding iterated-colimit isomorphism.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 0FND proof (line 9515), fourth equality

proof.text: For each $P$, morphisms in the left localization are computed, since the quasi-isomorphisms of the homotopy category form a multiplicative system, by the colimit over arrows $s:K\to I$: $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(G(P),K)\cong\varinjlim_{s:K\to I}\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(G(P),I)$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Lemma 0FND proof (line 9515), fifth equality

proof.text: Since $LG$ is defined at $M$, the pro-system $P\mapsto G(P)$ indexed by arrows $t:P\to M$ is essentially constant with value $LG(M)$. Applying the essential-constant pro Hom-colimit formula gives $\varinjlim_{t:P\to M}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(G(P),K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(LG(M),K)$.

statement_change.old_statement: Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be functors with $F$ right adjoint to $G$, and let $K$ be a complex of $\mathcal A$ and $M$ a complex of $\mathcal B$. Define $RF$ at $K$ when the ind-system of objects $F(K')$ in $D(\mathcal B)$, indexed by quasi-isomorphisms $K\to K'$ in $K(\mathcal A)$, is essentially constant with value $RF(K)$; define $LG$ at $M$ dually when the pro-system of objects $G(M')$ in $D(\mathcal A)$, indexed by quasi-isomorphisms $M'\to M$ in $K(\mathcal B)$, is essentially constant with value $LG(M)$. If $RF$ is defined at $K$ and $LG$ is defined at $M$, there is a canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal B)}(M,RF(K))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(LG(M),K)$, functorial in $K$ and $M$ on the triangulated subcategories where the respective derived functors are defined.
statement_change.what: The base leaves componentwise action on complexes implicit. Additivity (automatic from the abelian adjunction), homotopy objects, localization, and representing cone/cocone are now explicit. The first worker instead assumed an adjunction after localization and RF=F(K), LG=G(M); that circular correction is rejected and replaced by the source 0DVC construction. Canonicality and functoriality are stated on fraction representatives.
